### What does this PR do?

Add CPU contracts that follow Hermes and Kimi tool calls through the real parser, assistant-message construction, tool dispatch and reply assembly. Ten fixtures run through native tools and FunctionTool, checking IDs, invalid JSON, enabled/unknown tools, parallel limits, zero reward and reverse completion order.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [focused query](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Aopen%20%22tool_protocol_contract%22). Refreshed on 2026-10-17 against main `18cfb74852a0`.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

This tests the cross-stage protocol on current main. #6434 changes reasoning extraction, #7523 changes JSON Schema preservation, and #8156 changes BaseTool lifetime; none supplies this parser-to-reply contract suite. Existing tool-ID unit tests remain in the regression command.

### Test

Agent-run CPU validation: **73 passed**. The test command is:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_tool_protocol_contract_on_cpu.py tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_tool_call_id_on_cpu.py tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_call_tool_on_cpu.py tests/tools/test_function_tool_on_cpu.py tests/tools/test_mixed_tools_on_cpu.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Pre-commit: all 14 upstream hooks passed.

WSL Ubuntu, uv-managed Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.12.1, Ray 2.55.1. Installed CPU/test dependencies match the current uv.lock; Megatron-Core's source dependency was omitted. This is not a complete frozen environment or official CI/GPU result. The existing CPU workflow discovers the new `*_on_cpu.py` tests; no workflow change is required.

### API, Design and Boundaries

No runtime/API change. Tokenization, continuous-token construction and tool side effects are controlled substitutes; this does not validate a real model, token masks or training.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the implementation, documentation, tests and local execution evidence. The contributor confirmed reviewing this final diff and explicitly asked Codex to rerun the test command before publication. The rerun was executed by Codex; it is not described as a test command personally executed by the contributor.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md.
- [x] Apply all upstream pre-commit checks.
- [x] Update documentation and add CPU tests covered by the existing workflow.
- [x] Contributor confirmed reviewing the final diff.
- [x] Relevant tests rerun by Codex at the contributor's explicit request; execution is attributed above.
- [ ] Request CI through the upstream ci-request channel when ready. No message has been sent.

No recipe-submodule update applies. The contributor selected this work and authorized publication after review. The division between human review and agent-run testing is disclosed explicitly for maintainer assessment.

@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@
 Agent Loop
 ==========
 
-Last updated: 07/17/2025.
+Last updated: 10/17/2026.
 
 .. versionadded:: 0.4.2
    [status: alpha]
@@ -27,6 +27,56 @@ and return the final output. The final output is then calculated reward and used
 .. image:: https://github.com/eric-haibin-lin/verl-community/blob/main/docs/agent_loop_overview.svg?raw=true
 
 
+CPU tool protocol contracts
+---------------------------
+
+``tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_tool_protocol_contract_on_cpu.py`` replays
+the shared ``tool_protocol_cases.json`` corpus through the production parser,
+assistant-message builder, tool dispatcher and tool-reply builder. Each case
+runs with both a stateful native tool and a stateless ``FunctionTool``. This
+checks agreement between these stages, in addition to their focused unit tests.
+
+.. list-table:: Initial offline protocol coverage
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Contract
+     - Hermes
+     - Kimi
+   * - Text without tool calls
+     - Preserved
+     - Preserved
+   * - Arguments reaching the tool
+     - Nested values and Unicode preserved
+     - Objects preserved; invalid/non-object JSON falls back to an empty object
+   * - Malformed sibling call
+     - Skipped without dropping the valid sibling
+     - Uses the Kimi argument fallback above
+   * - Call IDs
+     - No model ID is invented
+     - Model ID preserved in assistant and tool messages
+   * - Dispatch boundaries
+     - Unknown tools rejected; parallel-call cap respected
+     - Tools outside the active selection are not executed
+
+Run the corpus on CPU using the repository's CPU environment::
+
+    uv run --frozen --all-packages --extra cpu pytest -q \
+        tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_tool_protocol_contract_on_cpu.py
+
+To extend a protocol, add a named case with its decoded text, expected content,
+arguments and optional model-emitted IDs. Record the format source in the
+corpus, and use that parser's error-recovery contract rather than making every
+parser reject the same inputs. New tool side effects should be represented by
+deterministic local test doubles.
+
+These are synthetic format fixtures, not recorded model generations. Decoding
+and Continuous Token context merging are explicit test doubles; the tests do
+not validate chat-template round trips, actual special-token IDs, backend stop
+conditions, generated-token masks or training convergence. Add separate tests
+with a fixed tokenizer revision and backend integration when claiming support
+for a new model. The parser must not replace the original response token IDs
+with a re-encoding of its reconstructed assistant message.
+
 API Design
 ----------

+"""Replay protocol fixtures through real parser, message assembly, dispatch and replies.
+
+Tokenizer decoding, Continuous Token merging, and tool side effects are test doubles.
+No inference backend, network service, model weights or global tool registry is used.
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import copy
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from verl.experimental.agent_loop.tool_agent_loop import AgentData, AgentState, ToolAgentLoop
+from verl.experimental.agent_loop.tool_parser import ToolParser
+from verl.tools.function_tool import FunctionTool
+from verl.tools.schemas import OpenAIFunctionToolSchema, ToolResponse
+
+_CORPUS = json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("tool_protocol_cases.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+
+def _schema(name):
+    return OpenAIFunctionToolSchema.model_validate(
+        {
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {
+                "name": name,
+                "description": "Offline protocol replay tool.",
+                "parameters": {
+                    "type": "object",
+                    "properties": {"value": {"type": ["object", "string", "integer"]}},
+                    "required": [],
+                },
+            },
+        }
+    )
+
+
+class _DecodedFixture:
+    def __init__(self, text):
+        self.text = text
+
+    def decode(self, token_ids, **kwargs):
+        assert token_ids == [21, 22, 23]
+        return self.text
+
+
+class _RecordingNativeTool:
+    def __init__(self, name, calls, lifecycle, complete):
+        self.name = name
+        self.tool_schema = _schema(name)
+        self.calls = calls
+        self.lifecycle = lifecycle
+        self.next_id = 0
+        self.complete = complete
+
+    async def create(self, create_kwargs):
+        instance_id = f"{self.name}-{self.next_id}"
+        self.next_id += 1
+        self.lifecycle.append(("create", instance_id))
+        return instance_id, ToolResponse()
+
+    async def execute(self, instance_id, parameters, **kwargs):
+        self.lifecycle.append(("execute", instance_id))
+        self.calls.append((self.name, copy.deepcopy(parameters)))
+        await self.complete(parameters)
+        return ToolResponse(text=json.dumps(parameters, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)), 0.0, {}
+
+    async def release(self, instance_id):
+        self.lifecycle.append(("release", instance_id))
+
+
+def _make_tools(kind, calls, lifecycle, complete):
+    tools = {}
+    for name in ("echo", "secret"):
+        if kind == "native":
+            tools[name] = _RecordingNativeTool(name, calls, lifecycle, complete)
+        else:
+
+            def make_function(tool_name):
+                async def invoke(**parameters):
+                    calls.append((tool_name, copy.deepcopy(parameters)))
+                    await complete(parameters)
+                    return json.dumps(parameters, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True), 0.0, {}
+
+                return invoke
+
+            tools[name] = FunctionTool(name, make_function(name), _schema(name), is_async=True)
+    return tools
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["native", "function"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", _CORPUS["cases"], ids=lambda case: case["id"])
+async def test_tool_protocol_reaches_dispatch_and_reply(case, kind):
+    calls, lifecycle = [], []
+    completions = []
+    second_done = asyncio.Event()
+
+    async def complete(parameters):
+        if case["id"] == "kimi-parallel-ids":
+            value = parameters["value"]
+            if value == "first":
+                await asyncio.wait_for(second_done.wait(), timeout=2)
+            completions.append(value)
+            if value == "second":
+                second_done.set()
+
+    loop = ToolAgentLoop.__new__(ToolAgentLoop)
+    loop.tools = _make_tools(kind, calls, lifecycle, complete)
+    loop.tool_schemas = [tool.tool_schema.model_dump() for tool in loop.tools.values()]
+    loop.max_parallel_calls = case.get("max_parallel_calls", 8)
+    loop.max_tool_response_length = 10000
+    loop.tool_response_truncate_side = "left"
+    loop.processor = None
+    loop.response_length = 128
+
+    # CT itself has separate tests. Preserve its inputs here; do not emulate tokenization
+    # or claim that round-tripping decoded fixture text reproduces model token IDs.
+    observed_contexts = []
+
+    async def merge_context(previous_messages, messages, token_ids, response_mask, response_logprobs, *, tools):
+        observed_contexts.append(copy.deepcopy(messages[len(previous_messages) :]))
+        return SimpleNamespace(token_ids=list(token_ids)), list(response_mask), response_logprobs
+
+    loop.ct_merge_context_msg = merge_context
+    loop._assert_mm_supported = lambda has_mm: None
+    agent_data = AgentData(
+        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Replay the fixture."}],
+        image_data=None,
+        video_data=None,
+        audio_data=None,
+        mm_processor_kwargs=None,
+        metrics={},
+        request_id="offline-protocol-fixture",
+        tools_kwargs={},
+    )
+    agent_data.prompt_ids = [10, 21, 22, 23]
+    agent_data.response_ids = [21, 22, 23]
+    agent_data.response_mask = [1, 1, 1]
+    agent_data.response_logprobs = [-0.1, -0.2, -0.3]
+    selected = case.get("active_tools", ["echo", "secret"])
+    agent_data._active_tools = {name: loop.tools[name] for name in selected}
+    agent_data._active_tool_schemas = [tool.tool_schema.model_dump() for tool in agent_data._active_tools.values()]
+    original_ids = list(agent_data.response_ids)
+
+    parser = ToolParser.get_tool_parser(case["parser"], _DecodedFixture(case["text"]))
+    content, parsed = await parser.extract_tool_calls(
+        agent_data.response_ids, [tool.tool_schema for tool in agent_data._active_tools.values()]
+    )
+    actual_calls = [
+        {"name": call.name, "arguments": json.loads(call.arguments), "tool_call_id": call.tool_call_id}
+        for call in parsed
+    ]
+    assert content == case["content"]
+    assert actual_calls == case["calls"]
+    agent_data.tool_calls = parsed
+
+    assistant = loop._build_assistant_message(content, agent_data)
+    agent_data.messages.append(assistant)
+    expected_calls = case["calls"][: loop.max_parallel_calls]
+    expected_messages = []
+    for call in expected_calls:
+        message = {"type": "function", "function": {"name": call["name"], "arguments": call["arguments"]}}
+        if call["tool_call_id"] is not None:
+            message["id"] = call["tool_call_id"]
+        expected_messages.append(message)
+    assert assistant == {
+        "role": "assistant",
+        "content": case["content"],
+        **({"tool_calls": expected_messages} if expected_messages else {}),
+    }
+
+    if parsed:
+        state = await loop._handle_processing_tools_state(agent_data)
+        assert state == AgentState.GENERATING
+        replies = agent_data.messages[2:]
+        assert len(replies) == len(expected_calls)
+        assert observed_contexts == [replies]
+        for call, reply in zip(expected_calls, replies, strict=True):
+            assert reply["role"] == "tool"
+            if call["tool_call_id"] is not None:
+                assert reply["tool_call_id"] == call["tool_call_id"]
+            else:
+                assert "tool_call_id" not in reply
+            if call["name"] in selected:
+                assert json.loads(reply["content"]) == call["arguments"]
+            else:
+                assert "Unknown function" in reply["content"]
+        assert agent_data.tool_rewards == [0.0] * len(expected_calls)
+    else:
+        assert observed_contexts == []
+
+    expected_executions = [(call["name"], call["arguments"]) for call in expected_calls if call["name"] in selected]
+    assert calls == expected_executions
+    if case["id"] == "kimi-parallel-ids":
+        assert completions == ["second", "first"]
+    if kind == "native":
+        created = [instance for event, instance in lifecycle if event == "create"]
+        assert len(created) == len(expected_executions)
+        for instance in created:
+            assert [event for event, key in lifecycle if key == instance] == ["create", "execute", "release"]
+    else:
+        assert lifecycle == []
+    assert agent_data.response_ids == original_ids
+    assert agent_data.prompt_ids == [10, 21, 22, 23]
+    assert agent_data.response_mask == [1, 1, 1]
+    assert agent_data.response_logprobs == [-0.1, -0.2, -0.3]

@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits.
